model_summary: A Gradient Boosted Decision Tree (GBDT) classifier for binary sleep apnea prediction, demonstrating how rural underdiagnosis bias causes a 47.4% rural recall collapse when models train on labels masked to simulate limited specialist access.
model_description: Two GradientBoostingClassifier models are trained on Synthea synthetic patient data: a baseline model trained on true sleep apnea labels and a biased model trained on observed labels where 30% of rural sleep apnea diagnoses are masked to simulate underdiagnosis. The case study quantifies how label masking bias — arising from rural populations' limited access to polysomnography and sleep specialists — propagates into clinical prediction models. Both models accept 9 clinical and demographic features (age, sex, urban/rural location, income, BMI, smoking status, hypertension, CHF, alcohol use disorder) and output a binary sleep apnea prediction. Evaluation against true labels reveals that the biased model's rural recall collapses from 30.65% to 16.13% (-47.4%) while urban recall improves, amplifying the urban–rural health disparity in model predictions. Aggregate AUC-ROC remains stable (0.6457 vs 0.6467), illustrating how ranking metrics can obscure critical subgroup inequity.
model_type: Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (GBDT), Supervised Learning, Tabular Classification
base_model: N/A — trained from scratch on Synthea synthetic patient data

uses.direct_use: This model is intended for educational and research use to demonstrate how rural underdiagnosis bias in training labels degrades predictive equity. It accepts 9 clinical and demographic features and outputs a binary sleep apnea prediction. The two model variants (baseline and biased) are designed to be compared, not deployed clinically.
uses.downstream_use: The pipeline can be adapted to study other forms of label masking bias in healthcare ML. The Synthea-based data generation can be modified to explore different mask rates, populations, or geographic stratifications. The framework generalizes to any condition with geography-dependent underdiagnosis.
uses.out_of_scope_use: This model must not be used for clinical diagnosis or patient triage. It is trained on fully synthetic data generated by the Synthea simulator and has not been validated on real patient populations. It is not suitable for production deployment in any healthcare setting.

bias_risks.bias_risks_limitations: The biased model exhibits substantial performance disparities between urban and rural subgroups. Rural recall falls from 30.65% to 16.13% (-47.4%), while urban recall rises from 42.37% to 47.33% (+11.7%). The recall gap between urban and rural patients widens from 11.7 to 31.2 percentage points. Aggregate AUC-ROC (0.6467) remains stable and masks these disparities entirely. The dataset is fully synthetic (Synthea), generated for a Vermont population aged 60–100 with seed 42; findings may not generalize to other geographies, demographics, or real clinical data. Sleep apnea prevalence (~9.4%) reflects Synthea simulation logic, not real-world epidemiology.
bias_risks.bias_recommendations: Always evaluate healthcare models on subgroup-specific recall metrics, not only aggregate AUC or accuracy. Investigate whether label completeness differs by geography, race, income, or insurance status before deployment. Apply sensitivity analysis across masking rates. Consider fairness-constrained training or post-processing corrections when systematic underdiagnosis is suspected in training data.

get_started_code:
import joblib
import pandas as pd

# Load a trained model
model = joblib.load('baseline_model.pkl')  # or 'biased_model.pkl'

# Prepare features (9 clinical/demographic inputs)
features = ['age', 'male', 'urban', 'income', 'bmi', 'smoker', 'hypertension', 'chf', 'alcohol_use']
X = pd.DataFrame([{
    'age': 68, 'male': 1, 'urban': 0, 'income': 0.42,
    'bmi': 32.1, 'smoker': 0, 'hypertension': 1, 'chf': 0, 'alcohol_use': 0
}])[features]

# Predict probability of sleep apnea
prob = model.predict_proba(X)[:, 1]
print(f'Sleep apnea probability: {prob[0]:.3f}')

training_details.training_data: Trained on Synthea synthetic patient data: 22,903 patients generated for Vermont with age range 60–100 and seed 42. Training set: 16,031 patients (1,512 positive for sleep apnea, 9.43% prevalence). Biased training set uses the same split with 117 rural positive labels masked to 0. Dataset card: https://github.com/synthetichealth/synthea
training_details.preprocessing: Features extracted from Synthea CSVs (patients.csv, conditions.csv, observations.csv). BMI imputed to 25.0 where missing. Income scaled by dividing by 100,000. Stratified 70/15/15 train/validation/test split maintaining class balance. Classification threshold selected by F1-score maximization on validation set (baseline: 0.1405, biased: 0.1233).
training_details.speeds_sizes_times: Training completed on CPU in under 1 minute. GradientBoostingClassifier: n_estimators=200, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.05, min_samples_split=20, min_samples_leaf=10, subsample=0.8, random_state=42. Two models trained (baseline + biased).

evaluation.testing_data: Test set: 3,436 patients (324 with true sleep apnea, 9.43% prevalence). Evaluation uses true labels for both models to measure real-world predictive accuracy. Urban subgroup: 2,793 patients; Rural subgroup: 643 patients.
evaluation.testing_factors: Performance evaluated overall and by urban/rural subgroup. Primary equity metric: recall disparity between urban and rural patients. Secondary factors: precision, F1, and AUC-ROC by subgroup.
evaluation.testing_metrics: Primary metrics: AUC-ROC, F1-score (at F1-optimal threshold), Recall, Precision, Accuracy. Additional: Average Precision (AP). All reported overall and for urban/rural subgroups.
evaluation.results: Baseline — Overall: AUC-ROC 0.6457, F1 0.2245, Recall 0.4012, Precision 0.1559, Accuracy 0.7386. Biased — Overall: AUC-ROC 0.6467, F1 0.2219, Recall 0.4136, Precision 0.1516, Accuracy 0.7264. Rural recall: 0.3065 → 0.1613 (-47.4%). Urban recall: 0.4237 → 0.4733 (+11.7%). Rural F1: 0.2135 → 0.1754 (-17.8%).
evaluation.results_summary: Aggregate metrics are nearly identical between baseline and biased models (ΔAUC-ROC < 0.001), yet the biased model catastrophically underserves rural patients: rural recall drops 47.4%, meaning nearly half of true rural sleep apnea cases go undetected. This demonstrates that stable aggregate ranking metrics can mask severe subgroup inequity caused by label masking bias.

technical_specs.model_specs: scikit-learn GradientBoostingClassifier: 200 estimators, max depth 5, learning rate 0.05, subsample 0.8, min_samples_split=20, min_samples_leaf=10. 9 input features, 1 binary output (sleep apnea present/absent).
technical_specs.compute_infrastructure: Standard CPU-based workstation. No GPU or cloud infrastructure required.
technical_specs.hardware_requirements: Minimal — any modern CPU with 2 GB RAM is sufficient for training and inference.

additional_info.glossary: **Label masking bias**: Systematic omission of true positive labels in training data due to underdiagnosis in specific populations. **Rural underdiagnosis**: Lower rates of formal diagnosis in rural populations due to limited specialist access. **Observed label**: What appears in medical records after masking — may differ from true condition status. **Recall collapse**: Dramatic drop in a model's true-positive detection rate for a subgroup.
